titulo_es: Specialised vocabulary: finance, diplomacy and international trade
descripcion_es: Terminology of finance, diplomacy and international trade.
resumen: Technical terminology that a Spanish Commercial Technician and State Economist (TCEE) needs in English: financial markets, monetary policy, trade negotiations, the WTO and economic diplomacy.

explicacion.texto: In specialised vocabulary, precision is essential: “tariff” and “duty” are almost perfect synonyms, but “quota” is something else; “yield” is not “rendimiento” in any sense, but the return on a bond. Learn each term with its usual collocation.

filas: bond / yield / spread
a debt security / the return on it / the difference between two yields, e.g. the risk premium (es: bono / rentabilidad / diferencial, prima de riesgo)
The spread over the Bund widened to 150 basis points.
basis point
one hundredth of a percentage point, 0.01% (es: punto básico)
Rates were cut by 25 basis points.
to default (on)
to fail to make debt payments (es: impagar, entrar en impago)
The country defaulted on its debt.
bailout / bail-in
a rescue with outside funds / an internal recapitalisation at creditors’ expense (es: rescate con fondos externos / recapitalización interna)
The bailout came with strict conditions.
quantitative easing (QE)
large-scale asset purchases by a central bank (es: expansión cuantitativa)
The ECB launched QE in 2015.
to tighten / loosen monetary policy
to make monetary policy stricter / less strict (es: endurecer / relajar la política monetaria)
The Fed began tightening in 2022.
hedge / hedging
protection against a financial risk (es: cobertura de riesgos)
Firms use futures to hedge currency risk.
leverage
the use of borrowed money to increase exposure (es: apalancamiento)
Banks reduced leverage after the crisis.
capital requirements
the minimum capital that banks must hold (es: requisitos de capital)
Basel III raised capital requirements.
sovereign debt / credit rating
government debt / an assessment of creditworthiness (es: deuda soberana / calificación crediticia)
The agency downgraded the country's credit rating.
current account balance
the balance of trade in goods, services and income (es: saldo por cuenta corriente)
Spain has a current account surplus.
exchange rate / to peg
the price of one currency in another / to fix a currency to another (es: tipo de cambio / vincular una divisa)
The currency is pegged to the dollar.
tariff / duty
a tax on imports / a customs charge (es: arancel / derecho de aduana)
Duties on cars were reduced to 10%.
quota / tariff-rate quota
a quantitative limit / a quantity imported at a lower tariff (es: contingente / contingente arancelario)
Imports above the quota face higher duties.
non-tariff barriers
trade restrictions other than tariffs (es: barreras no arancelarias)
Standards can act as non-tariff barriers.
most-favoured-nation (MFN) treatment
giving all partners the best treatment granted to any country (es: trato de nación más favorecida)
WTO members grant MFN treatment to each other.
anti-dumping duties
extra duties on imports sold below normal value (es: derechos antidumping)
The EU imposed anti-dumping duties on steel.
rules of origin
criteria that determine where a product comes from (es: normas de origen)
Rules of origin determine eligibility for preferences.
free trade agreement (FTA)
a treaty that removes trade barriers between parties (es: acuerdo de libre comercio)
The EU signed an FTA with Mercosur.
dispute settlement
the procedure for resolving trade disputes (es: solución de diferencias)
The case went to WTO dispute settlement.
export credit
financing or insurance that supports exports (es: crédito a la exportación)
Export credit agencies support exporters.
foreign direct investment (FDI)
a lasting investment in a company abroad (es: inversión extranjera directa, IED)
FDI inflows rose by 20%.
to ratify / ratification
to give formal approval to a treaty / the act of doing so (es: ratificar / ratificación)
The treaty has not yet been ratified.
memorandum of understanding (MoU)
a non-binding written agreement (es: memorando de entendimiento)
Both ministries signed an MoU.
envoy / ambassador / attaché
a diplomatic representative / the head of an embassy / an embassy specialist (es: enviado / embajador / agregado)
The commercial attaché organised the trade mission.
bilateral / multilateral talks
negotiations between two / many parties (es: negociaciones bilaterales / multilaterales)
Multilateral talks have stalled.
sanctions / to impose sanctions
penalties against a country / to apply them (es: sanciones / imponer sanciones)
The EU imposed sanctions on the regime.

items: “Commercial attaché” is the trade attaché (es: agregado comercial); the Spanish “Oficina Económica y Comercial” is usually translated as “Economic and Commercial Office”.
“Default” is not a defect: it is non-payment (es: impago); “by default” = automatically, without a choice (es: por defecto).
“Rating” goes with “downgrade / upgrade”: to lower / raise the rating.

ejemplos.frase: Ten-year bond yields rose sharply after the announcement.
ejemplos.traduccion: La rentabilidad del bono a diez años subió con fuerza tras el anuncio.

ejemplos.frase: The rating agency downgraded the bank to junk status.
ejemplos.traduccion: La agencia de calificación rebajó al banco a la categoría de bono basura.

ejemplos.frase: The EU and Japan agreed to phase out most tariffs over ten years.
ejemplos.traduccion: La UE y Japón acordaron eliminar gradualmente la mayoría de los aranceles en diez años.

ejemplos.frase: Exporters hedge against currency fluctuations with forward contracts.
ejemplos.traduccion: Los exportadores se cubren frente a las fluctuaciones de divisas con contratos a plazo.

ejemplos.frase: The agreement will enter into force once all parties have ratified it.
ejemplos.traduccion: El acuerdo entrará en vigor cuando todas las partes lo hayan ratificado.

ejemplos.frase: The ambassador was summoned to the foreign ministry.
ejemplos.traduccion: El embajador fue convocado al Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The risk premium went up to 150 points.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The spread widened to 150 basis points.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The risk premium (es: prima de riesgo) is “spread” (or “risk premium”), and it is measured in “basis points”.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The country made a default of its debt.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The country defaulted on its debt.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: “Default” is used as a verb with “on”.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The agency lowered the qualification of Spain.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The agency downgraded Spain's credit rating.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: A credit rating (es: calificación crediticia) is a “credit rating”, and it is “downgraded”.

ejercicios.frase: The ECB cut rates by 25 ___ points.
ejercicios.explicacion: The key expression, listed in the table on this card, is basis point: one hundredth of a percentage point (0.01%). The clue is the monetary policy context (the ECB cut rates) and the figure of 25, typical of interest rate decisions: 25 basis points equal 0.25 percentage points. Basis is a noun used here as a modifier and does not allow variants such as base or basic.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The Spanish “punto básico” is a “basis point” (0.01%).
ejercicios.traduccion: El BCE bajó los tipos 25 puntos básicos.

por_opcion.basis: Correct: basis point is the established term for 0.01%.
por_opcion.base: Incorrect: base means a foundation or headquarters (a military base, the tax base), but the term is not “base point”.
por_opcion.percentage: Incorrect: percentage points are whole points; a cut of 25 percentage points would be absurd.
por_opcion.basic: Incorrect: basic is an adjective (“fundamental, elementary”), as in basic needs; it is a literal copy of the Spanish “puntos básicos”.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with a verb (to fail to pay a debt), in the past.
ejercicios.frase: Argentina ___ on its sovereign debt several times.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that default, used as a verb with the preposition on, means to fail to pay a debt (es: impagar, entrar en impago), and has nothing to do with a defect. The clue is the preposition on and the object sovereign debt: default on a debt is the fixed collocation. The instruction asks for the past, hence defaulted; in both British and American English has defaulted would also be used, but the gap is for a single verb form.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Default on” = to fail to pay (es: impagar).
ejercicios.traduccion: Argentina ha impagado su deuda soberana varias veces.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Unpaid is an adjective (unpaid bills); it does not work as a verb with on.
Failed on is not the collocation; you could say failed to pay its debt, but the technical term is defaulted on.
The instruction asks for the verb in the past: defaulted.

glosario.significado: impagar, entrar en impago (de una deuda)
por defecto (no confundir con el impago)

ejercicios.frase: Moody's lowered the qualification of the bank to junk.
respuestas: Moody's downgraded the bank to junk.
Moody's lowered the bank's rating to junk.
Moody's downgraded the bank's rating to junk.
Moody's lowered the rating of the bank to junk.
Moody's downgraded the rating of the bank to junk.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains in Rules and key points that a credit rating is rating and that lowering it is downgrade (raising it, upgrade). The clue is the agency (Moody's) and the destination junk, the junk bond level. Qualification means a diploma or a requirement, so it is a false friend. Several answers are valid: the verb downgrade applied to the bank or to its rating, or lowered with rating; all of them replace qualification with the correct term.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A credit rating is a “rating”; lowering it is “downgrade”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Moody's rebajó la calificación del banco a bono basura.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Moody's lowered the qualification of the bank to junk.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: qualification is a diploma or a requirement, not a credit rating.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Moody's downgraded the qualification of the bank to junk.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The verb is now correct, but the false friend qualification is still there; you need rating.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Moody's lowered the note of the bank to junk.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Note is a written note or a banknote, not a credit rating; the term is rating.

glosario.significado: basura; aquí, categoría de bono basura (por debajo del grado de inversión)
titulación, cualificación o requisito (falso amigo de «calificación»)

ejercicios.frase: WTO members must grant each other most-favoured-___ treatment.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table on this card lists most-favoured-nation (MFN) treatment: each member must give the others the most advantageous treatment it grants to any country. The clue is the WTO and the structure most-favoured-___ treatment, a fixed GATT term. Although country or state are synonyms in everyday language, the legal term only allows nation.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los miembros de la OMC deben concederse mutuamente el trato de nación más favorecida.

por_opcion.nation: Correct: most-favoured-nation treatment is the official name of the principle (abbreviated MFN).
por_opcion.country: Incorrect: country is a synonym in general use, but “most-favoured-country” is not the established term.
por_opcion.state: Incorrect: state is not part of this term; it is used in Member State or state aid.
por_opcion.partner: Incorrect: partner is used in trading partner, but it is not part of the name of the principle.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with one word (the difference between two bond yields).
ejercicios.frase: The ___ between Spanish and German bonds narrowed to 80 basis points.
ejercicios.explicacion: According to the card, the yield difference or risk premium (es: diferencial, prima de riesgo) is spread: the difference in yield between two bonds. The clue is the structure “the ___ between Spanish and German bonds” and the measurement in basis points. The verb narrow is the usual collocation of spread, together with widen. Risk premium also exists, but it does not fit this collocation with between.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The yield difference or risk premium (es: diferencial, prima de riesgo) is the “spread”.
ejercicios.traduccion: El diferencial entre los bonos españoles y alemanes se estrechó hasta los 80 puntos básicos.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Differential exists in English (interest rate differential), but the difference between the yields of two bonds is called spread.
Difference is the general word; the technical term in debt markets is spread.
Premium alone does not name this concept; it would be risk premium, and with between you use spread.

ejercicios.frase: The Commission imposed anti-___ duties on Chinese solar panels.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table on this card lists anti-dumping duties: additional tariffs on imports sold below their normal value. The clue is anti- and duties: the fixed term uses the noun dumping, the practice of selling abroad below the price. Neither the verb dump nor the participle dumped can follow the prefix in this term.
ejercicios.traduccion: La Comisión impuso derechos antidumping a los paneles solares chinos.

por_opcion.dumping: Correct: anti-dumping duties is the technical term in trade defence.
por_opcion.damping: Incorrect: damping is the reduction of vibrations or oscillations; confusing it with dumping is a spelling mistake that changes the meaning.
por_opcion.dump: Incorrect: dump is the verb (to discard, to sell at a loss) or a noun meaning a rubbish tip; it does not form the term anti-dump.
por_opcion.dumped: Incorrect: dumped is the participle; you would say dumped imports, but not anti-dumped duties.

ejercicios.frase: Foreign direct inversion in Spain reached a record high.
respuestas: Foreign direct investment in Spain reached a record high.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the false friend that the card lists among the typical mistakes: “inversión” in the economic sense is investment, and the Spanish IED is foreign direct investment (FDI). Inversion in English means turning something the other way round (an inversion of word order or of the yield curve, yield curve inversion). The clue is the phrase foreign direct, which forms a fixed term with investment.
ejercicios.traduccion: La inversión extranjera directa en España alcanzó un máximo histórico.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Foreign direct inversion in Spain reached a record high.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: inversion means turning upside down or reversing the order, not capital investment.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Foreign direct investments in Spain reached a record high.
errores_previstos.explicacion: In the term FDI, investment is singular, as an uncountable noun; the plural is used for specific investments, not for the aggregate.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Direct foreign inversion in Spain reached a record high.
errores_previstos.explicacion: As well as keeping the false friend, it changes the fixed order of the term foreign direct investment.

glosario.significado: inversión en el sentido de dar la vuelta (falso amigo)

ejercicios.frase: Exporters use forward contracts to ___ against exchange-rate risk.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card lists hedge / hedging as protection against risks: hedge against a risk means protecting yourself from it. The clue is forward contracts (the classic hedging instrument) and the preposition against. Edge, hide and cover up are similar in form or in general meaning, but none of them is the financial term.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Hedge against” = to protect yourself from a risk.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los exportadores utilizan contratos a plazo para cubrirse frente al riesgo de tipo de cambio.

por_opcion.hedge: Correct: hedge against = to protect yourself from a risk; it is the financial term.
por_opcion.edge: Incorrect: edge is a border or an advantage (a competitive edge); it looks similar but does not mean protecting yourself.
por_opcion.hide: Incorrect: hide means to conceal (yourself); it has no financial meaning.
por_opcion.cover up: Incorrect: cover up means to conceal something shameful (a scandal); for risks you would say cover against or, better, hedge.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with one word (the criteria that determine where a product comes from).
ejercicios.frase: Goods must meet the rules of ___ to benefit from lower tariffs.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table on this card lists rules of origin, which determine the economic nationality of a product and, therefore, whether it qualifies for the preferences of a trade agreement. The clue is the collocation meet the rules of ___ and the tariff benefit. Origin is the noun; original is an adjective and does not fit here.
ejercicios.traduccion: Las mercancías deben cumplir las normas de origen para beneficiarse de aranceles más bajos.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Original is an adjective; the term needs the noun origin.
This is the Spanish word; in English it is origin.
Provenance means where something comes from (a work of art, for example), but the customs term is rules of origin.

ejercicios.frase: The Danish krone is ___ to the euro.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card lists to peg: to fix the exchange rate of one currency to another. The clue is the currency (Danish krone), the reference (the euro) and the preposition to: a currency is pegged to another. It is the technical term for a fixed or semi-fixed exchange rate, such as that of the Danish krone within ERM II.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Peg a currency” = to fix its exchange rate to another.
ejercicios.traduccion: La corona danesa está vinculada al euro.

por_opcion.pegged: Correct: pegged to = fixed to; it is the technical term for exchange rate regimes.
por_opcion.pinned: Incorrect: pinned means fastened with pins or held in place; it is not used for currencies.
por_opcion.hooked: Incorrect: hooked means caught on a hook or addicted (hooked on); it has no exchange rate meaning.
por_opcion.tied up: Incorrect: tied up means tied or busy (my money is tied up = my money is not available); you say tied to for “linked to”, but not tied up.

glosario.significado: vincular el tipo de cambio (de una divisa)

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with one word (the procedure for resolving trade disputes).
ejercicios.frase: The EU took the case to the WTO's dispute ___ body.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table on this card lists dispute settlement (es: solución de diferencias); the WTO body is the Dispute Settlement Body. The clue is dispute ___ body and the context of a dispute between the EU and another member. Settlement comes from settle (to resolve, to put an end to) and is the noun that forms the term.
ejercicios.traduccion: La UE llevó el caso al Órgano de Solución de Diferencias de la OMC.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Solution is the answer to a problem; for trade disputes the fixed term is settlement.
Dispute resolution exists in general English, but the WTO body is called the Dispute Settlement Body.
Settle is the verb; the term needs the noun settlement.

ejercicios.frase: Imports within the ___ pay a reduced tariff; above it, the full rate applies.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card distinguishes quota from tariff and duty, and lists the tariff-rate quota. The clue is the description of the mechanism: a reduced tariff within a volume and the full rate above it, which is exactly a tariff-rate quota. The Spanish word “cuota” is misleading: in English quota is a quantitative limit, while share is a market share and quote is a price quotation.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The Spanish “contingente arancelario” is a “tariff-rate quota”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Las importaciones dentro del contingente pagan un arancel reducido; por encima de él se aplica el tipo completo.

por_opcion.quota: Correct: quota is a quantitative limit; within it the reduced tariff applies.
por_opcion.cuota: Incorrect: this is the Spanish word; it does not exist in English.
por_opcion.share: Incorrect: share is a part or stake (market share), not an import quota.
por_opcion.quote: Incorrect: quote is a quotation or a price estimate (a price quote), not a quota.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with a verb (to give formal approval to a treaty), as a past participle.
ejercicios.frase: The treaty will enter into force once it has been ___ by all Member States.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card lists to ratify / ratification: to give formal approval to a treaty. The clue is has been ___ by, a present perfect passive that requires the past participle (ratified), and the expression enter into force, typical of treaty language. The final y of ratify changes to i before -ed.
ejercicios.traduccion: El tratado entrará en vigor una vez que lo hayan ratificado todos los Estados miembros.

errores_previstos.explicacion: After has been you need the past participle: ratified.
Verbs ending in consonant + y change the y to i: ratified.
Approved is possible in other contexts, but the instruction asks for the verb meaning to ratify: ratified.

ejercicios.frase: After the crisis, regulators raised capital ___ for banks.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table on this card lists capital requirements, the minimum capital that banks must hold (for example, under Basel III). The clue is the subject regulators and the verb raise: what is raised is the regulatory requirements. Requisites is a rarely used literal copy; requests and demands are petitions, not regulatory obligations.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tras la crisis, los supervisores elevaron los requisitos de capital de los bancos.

por_opcion.requirements: Correct: capital requirements is the regulatory term.
por_opcion.requests: Incorrect: requests are petitions or applications, not regulatory obligations.
por_opcion.requisites: Incorrect: requisite exists but is rare and formal (“something essential”); it is not used in this term and is a literal copy of the Spanish “requisitos”.
por_opcion.demands of: Incorrect: demands are claims or calls for something, and the preposition of does not fit after raised capital.

respuestas: The EU imposed sanctions on Russia
ejercicios.explicacion: The card lists impose sanctions on. The key is the preposition on, which corresponds to the Spanish “a” (“imponer sanciones a”): the country sanctioned goes after on. The order is subject (The EU), verb (imposed), object (sanctions) and on + recipient (Russia). The capital T in The shows that the sentence begins with The EU.
ejercicios.traduccion: La UE impuso sanciones a Rusia.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The EU imposed on Russia sanctions
errores_previstos.explicacion: This order copies the Spanish (“impuso a Rusia sanciones”); in English the direct object comes before the phrase with on.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The EU sanctions imposed on Russia
errores_previstos.explicacion: This forms a noun phrase (“the EU sanctions imposed on Russia”), not a sentence with a main verb.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Russia imposed sanctions on the EU
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is grammatical, but it ignores the capital T in The, which marks the beginning of the sentence: The EU is the subject that imposes the sanctions.

descripcion_larga_es: This card brings together English terminology for finance, monetary policy, international trade, the WTO and economic diplomacy: spread, basis point, default, hedge, quota, rules of origin, dispute settlement. For a Commercial Technician and State Economist this is everyday working vocabulary, and false friends (inversion, qualification, cuota) can change the meaning of a report or a negotiation.

contexto.que_es: It is the technical vocabulary, with its fixed collocations, used in financial markets, central banks, trade negotiations and international organisations. Many terms have no word-for-word translation: the Spanish “prima de riesgo” is spread, “impago” is default and “contingente arancelario” is tariff-rate quota.
contexto.por_que_importa: In a TCEE's work these terms appear in reports, ECB or Commission press releases and negotiations with other countries, as well as in the language exam of the competitive examination. A terminological mistake is not just a matter of style: confusing quota with share or inversion with investment can make a text say something else or cost the author credibility with an expert counterpart.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: It is used when reading or writing economic texts, summarising financial news, translating foreign trade documents or in bilateral meetings. The signals are the field (bonds, tariffs, treaties) and the collocations: cut rates by X basis points, default on, hedge against, impose sanctions on. Spanish speakers tend to copy the Spanish word (inversion, qualification, cuota), and this card teaches the established English form.
